title.rendered: Rescue of abducted pupils victory for Nigeria, says Oyo senator

content.rendered:
The senator representing Oyo North Senatorial District, Abdulfatai Buhari, has described the rescue of 44 abducted schoolchildren and their teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State as a victory for Nigerians and the country’s security architecture.

Buhari, in a statement issued in Ibadan on Saturday, also commended President Bola Tinubu and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde for working closely with security agencies to secure the victims’ release.

He said, “The successful release of the 44 abducted schoolchildren and their teachers was made possible by the steadfast dedication and coordinated efforts of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Seyi Makinde, working in collaboration with the Nigerian security agencies.

“On behalf of the good people of Oyo North Senatorial District, particularly Oriire Local Government Area, I thank President Bola Tinubu for his decisive leadership and prompt directives that ensured no stone was left unturned in securing the release of our children and their teachers.

“The freedom of these 44 abducted schoolchildren and their teachers in Oriire Local Government is a victory for all Nigerians and the nation’s security architecture.”

PUNCH Online reports that more than 40 schoolchildren and their teachers were abducted during coordinated attacks on Baptist Nursery and Primary School, Yawota; L.A. Primary School; and Community Grammar School, Esiele, in Oriire Local Government Area on May 15, 2026. They regained their freedom on July 10, 2026, after spending 56 days in captivity.

Buhari also praised Makinde for his hands-on approach, constant engagement with stakeholders and the support provided by the state government throughout the period of the victims’ captivity.

The lawmaker specifically commended the Nigerian Army, the Department of State Services, the Nigeria Police Force, the Western Nigeria Security Network, codenamed Amotekun, vigilantes and local hunters for their bravery, professionalism and sacrifice.

He said, “The officers on the ground displayed patriotism and resilience. Their commitment in the bush, on the highways and in intelligence gathering led to this successful outcome.”

The senator rejoiced with the families of the victims, noting that the period of uncertainty had been painful for the entire senatorial district, Oyo State and the country.

He urged the families to remain strong and continue supporting one another as the victims begin their recovery, while praying for their speedy recovery and sound health.

“The government and relevant agencies will continue to monitor their well-being. This is not the end. The victims will receive further government attention, medical support and psychosocial care to help them fully reintegrate into society,” he assured.

Buhari also called on residents of Oyo North to remain vigilant and continue cooperating with security agencies.

He reaffirmed his commitment to working with the Federal Government and the Oyo State Government to strengthen security and ensure that similar incidents do not recur in any part of the senatorial district.
